title: Lands End Coastal Trail
blurb: Cypress cliffs, the Golden Gate from the side nobody photographs, and a stone labyrinth at the edge of the city.
best: Golden hour, and low tide for the Mile Rock Beach stairs.
tip: It's colder than the rest of the city out here. Bring the layer you think you won't need.

title: Sutro Baths ruins
blurb: Concrete bones of a glass bathhouse that once held six saltwater pools. Walk the edges at low tide.
best: Sunset, when the ruins go gold.
tip: Peek into the sea cave at the north end, carefully.

title: Batteries to Bluffs Trail
blurb: A short, steep staircase trail down to Marshall's Beach with the bridge filling the whole frame.
best: Clear mornings before the fog.
tip: The stairs back up are the workout. Go slow.

title: Mount Sutro Cloud Forest
blurb: Fog drips off the eucalyptus like rain. A mossy forest loop ten minutes from the N Judah.
best: Foggy mornings, when it actually feels like a cloud forest.
tip: It's muddy after rain. Wear shoes you don't love.

title: Twin Peaks summit
blurb: The whole city laid out like a map, from the Bay Bridge to the ocean.
best: Just after sunset, when the grid lights up.
tip: Windy year-round. Walk up from Clarendon Ave to skip the tour buses.

title: Bernal Heights summit
blurb: A bald hill with dogs, swings and a 360-degree view. Locals come up for sunrise.
best: Sunrise, or a clear evening.
tip: The rope swing on the east side moves around. Ask a dog walker.

title: Corona Heights
blurb: A rocky red outcrop over the Castro with one of the best downtown views.
best: Late afternoon light on downtown.
tip: Scramble the rocks at the very top for the full view.

title: Tank Hill
blurb: A tiny, quiet hilltop with a bench and a view most people never find.
best: Weeknight sunsets, when you'll likely have it to yourself.

title: 16th Avenue Tiled Steps
blurb: 163 mosaic steps that run from sea creatures to the sun, made by neighbors.
best: Morning, then keep climbing to Grandview Park.
tip: Grandview Park at the top has an ocean-to-bay view.

title: Sunset at Ocean Beach
blurb: Four miles of wide beach, surfers, and fire pits where strangers share the warmth.
best: Sunset. The fire pits fill up on clear weekends.
tip: Swimming here is dangerous. Watch, don't swim.

title: Baker Beach
blurb: The classic Golden Gate beach view, with old battery bunkers behind the dunes.
best: Late afternoon.
tip: The north end is clothing-optional. Now you know.

title: Crissy Field walk
blurb: Flat bayfront path with kites, dogs and the bridge growing bigger the whole way.
best: Morning, before the wind picks up.

title: Fort Point, under the bridge
blurb: A Civil War-era brick fort tucked directly under the Golden Gate Bridge.
best: Big swell days, when waves crash over the seawall.
tip: Touch the fence at the end of the pier. Everyone does.

title: Walk across the Golden Gate Bridge
blurb: 1.7 miles each way, 220 feet over the water, foghorns included.
best: Early morning, before the crowds.
tip: The east sidewalk is for walkers. It's loud and windy; that's the point.

title: Paddle Stow Lake
blurb: Rent a pedal boat, circle Strawberry Hill and the waterfall in the middle of the park.
best: Weekday afternoons.
tip: Walk up Strawberry Hill for the Huntington Falls view.

title: Bison in Golden Gate Park
blurb: A small herd of bison has lived in the park since the 1890s. Yes, really.
best: Morning, when they're out by the fence.

title: A sunny afternoon in Dolores Park
blurb: The city's living room. Sit on the hill, watch downtown, talk to whoever's next to you.
best: Warm weekend afternoons.
tip: The upper southwest corner has the view.

title: Alamo Square and the Painted Ladies
blurb: The row of Victorians from every postcard, with downtown behind them.
best: Late afternoon light on the houses.

title: Hear the Wave Organ
blurb: Pipes in a jetty that play the bay. Granite from an old cemetery makes the seats.
best: High tide, when it actually sounds.
tip: Check a tide chart first. At low tide it's mostly quiet.

title: Swim at Aquatic Park
blurb: Cold-water swimmers go year-round in this sheltered cove. Dip in, or just watch.
best: Morning, with the regulars.
tip: The water's in the 50s. Five minutes counts.

title: Glen Canyon Park
blurb: A real canyon with a creek and climbing rocks, hidden in the middle of the city.
best: Any morning.

title: Seward Street Slides
blurb: Two concrete slides down a hillside, designed by a 14-year-old in the 1970s.
best: Any day it's dry.
tip: Bring cardboard. You'll go faster than you think.

title: Fort Funston bluffs
blurb: Sand cliffs, hang gliders overhead, and the happiest dogs in the city.
best: Windy afternoons, when the gliders are up.
tip: The sand ladder down to the beach is steep both ways.

title: Presidio Tunnel Tops
blurb: Lawns built over the highway tunnels, with a bay view, a campfire circle and food trucks.
best: Sunny weekends, when the picnics come out.

title: Lyon Street Steps
blurb: Hedge-lined stairs between mansions with the Palace of Fine Arts and the bay below.
best: Morning. Locals do laps here.
tip: Count the steps. There are 332.

title: Filbert Steps to Coit Tower
blurb: Garden stairways past cottages and wild parrots, up to the tower and its murals.
best: Morning, when the parrots are loud.
tip: Start from Sansome St and climb up, not down.

title: Saturday at the Ferry Plaza market
blurb: The city's big farmers market, with bay views and a building full of food behind it.
best: Saturday morning, before 10.
tip: Walk the back side along the water first; that's where the farmers are.

title: A Mission burrito at La Taqueria
blurb: No rice, crisped on the plancha if you ask. The argument starter.
tip: Order it dorado style. Cash is easiest.

title: Morning bun at Tartine
blurb: The bakery that taught the city about sourdough. Get the morning bun and walk to Dolores Park.
best: Early, before the line wraps the corner.

title: Fortune cookies in Ross Alley
blurb: Watch cookies folded by hand in a tiny alley factory, then walk the rest of Chinatown.
tip: Bring a little cash for a bag of warm ones.

title: Irish coffee at the Buena Vista
blurb: The bar that brought Irish coffee to America, lined up a dozen glasses at a time.
best: Afternoon, after the cable car ride.
tip: Grab a window seat by the cable car turnaround.

title: Bi-Rite Creamery, then the park
blurb: Salted caramel in a cone, carried half a block to the Dolores Park hill.
best: Sunny afternoons. The line moves fast.

title: Swan Oyster Depot
blurb: A marble counter, eighteen stools and a family that's run it for generations.
best: Weekday, right at opening.
tip: Ask for the Sicilian sashimi.

title: Japanese Tea Garden
blurb: The oldest public Japanese garden in the country, with a steep drum bridge and tea house.
best: Right at opening, when it's quiet.

title: Conservatory of Flowers
blurb: A white Victorian glasshouse full of orchids, carnivorous plants and humid air.
tip: The lawn out front is one of the park's best sunbathing spots.

title: City Lights Bookstore
blurb: The Beat-era bookstore. Go upstairs to the poetry room and sit in the window.
tip: Jack Kerouac Alley next door has poems set in the pavement.

title: Musée Mécanique
blurb: A free hall of antique arcade machines, fortune tellers and player pianos that still work.
tip: Bring quarters. Laffing Sal will greet you.

title: Exploratorium After Dark
blurb: The science museum where you touch everything, adults-only on Thursday nights.
best: Thursday nights, 18 and up.
tip: Find the Tactile Dome. Book it ahead.

title: Balmy Alley murals
blurb: A whole alley of murals, painted over decades by the neighborhood.
tip: Walk on to Precita Eyes on 24th St to learn who painted what.

title: Clarion Alley
blurb: A block of constantly changing street art between Mission and Valencia.
best: Daylight, then dinner on Valencia.

title: Ride a cable car, Powell–Hyde line
blurb: Hang off the side over Russian Hill with the bay and Alcatraz dropping into view.
best: Early morning, before the turnaround line forms.
tip: Ride the Hyde St side, standing on the running board.

title: Palace of Fine Arts
blurb: A crumbling-looking Roman rotunda by a swan lagoon, built for a 1915 world's fair.
best: Dusk, when the rotunda is lit.

title: Legion of Honor
blurb: A hilltop art museum with Rodin's Thinker in the courtyard and the bridge out back.
tip: Pair it with the Lands End trail, which passes right below.

title: Walk the labyrinth at Grace Cathedral
blurb: A stone labyrinth outside and one inside a Gothic cathedral on top of Nob Hill.
best: Evening, when the outdoor one is quiet.

title: Mission Dolores
blurb: The oldest building in San Francisco, finished in 1791, with a small cemetery garden.
tip: The ceiling is painted in Ohlone patterns. Look up.

title: A movie at the Castro Theatre
blurb: A 1922 movie palace with an organ that rises out of the floor before the show.
tip: Sing-alongs here are a real event. Check the calendar.

title: A rainstorm at the Tonga Room
blurb: A tiki bar in an old hotel pool, where the band floats on a barge and it rains on schedule.
best: Weeknights, around the half-hour storms.

title: A night at SFJAZZ
blurb: A glass-walled jazz hall where every seat is close. Smaller rooms run late sets.
tip: The Joe Henderson Lab upstairs is the intimate one.

title: A show at the Fillmore
blurb: The legendary ballroom. They still hand out free apples at the door.
tip: Grab a poster on the way out after sold-out shows.

title: Watch the Giants from the Portwalk
blurb: Free standing room behind right field, looking through the fence onto the field.
best: Game nights, early innings.
tip: Watch for kayaks in McCovey Cove waiting for home runs.
